notThisReview: This is a DR-103 corpus review. It did not touch the frozen DR-112 v7 verdict, the frozen permission-truth-tables.v5 verdict, or any DR-111 artifact.
verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: Both of my v3 findings are repaired, and the repair method is the right one for a frozen-bytes corpus: rather than mutating the fixture I objected to, v4 authors new bytes under fixtures/dr-103.v4/ and retargets only its own entry, recording the v2 predecessor path and digest alongside it. I verified the substance rather than the description. The unicode-norm-duplicate replacement now carries bin/entry in its committed tree, so the entrypoint-presence rule can no longer fire and the NFC/NFD pair — bin/café at c3a9 against bin/café at 65cc81 — is the sole remaining violation, which is exactly the remedy I specified. The parity mismatch arm is real: the same pinned index carrying [help, version, doctor] is set against a new divergent observation carrying [help, version, doctor, analyze], the packet's recorded liveGrammarDigest reproduces against those bytes, and the expectation is REFUSE, so a checker that never compares now fails a fixture. On the integrity side the corpus is clean at the byte level: all 52 authored fixtures and all 32 supporting files reproduce against their recorded digests with zero mismatches and zero missing, and I proved fixtures/dr-103.v2/ unmutated by re-measuring all 162 pins that the two frozen predecessor corpora record against it. No lock fixture is scored while DR-111 is open. The two advisories are wording, one of them inherited unchanged since corpus v2.

advisories.title: An inherited notAuthored line says the corpus 'produces' an exact-pin lock, which the accepted schema and this corpus's own authorityClaim both deny
advisories.detail: The entry reads 'deferred until DR-111; v4 only produces dependency-free single-component exact-pin'. The fixture it refers to, TC-ACCEPT.lock-single-component, is in deferredUntilDR111 with standing DEFERRED-UNTIL-DR-111 and a note saying 'No lock fixture is required or producible until DR-111. Bytes retained as supporting, not scored', and I confirmed it is absent from authored[]. So nothing is produced or scored. The word sits against three other statements in the same document — that note, whatThisDoesNotDo's 'Does not score or require a lock fixture while DR-111 remains OPEN', and authorityClaim's 'Does not make any lock producible' — and against the D-104 schema's own position that no lock of any form, exact-pin included, is producible until DR-111 closes.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The dispatched attack is a scored lock fixture, and there is none: the structural facts are unambiguous and point the safe way. The line is also not this generation's work — I measured it byte-identical in corpus v2, v3 and v4, so it has been inherited unchanged across three generations and predates my v3 review, where I did not flag it. I raise it now because a SATISFIED-grade corpus is exactly the document someone could later quote out of context as evidence that a lock was produced.
advisories.suggestedFix: Reword to 'deferred until DR-111; the dependency-free single-component exact-pin bytes are retained as deferred supporting evidence, not produced or scored', in a successor rather than by editing frozen predecessors.

Unlike the sibling lineages, this roster makes no universal closure claim — its only closure sentence is the narrow 'Every other authored path/digest is unchanged from v3', and I verified that claim holds exactly: keying by fixture id rather than array position, TC-PATH.unicode-norm-duplicate is the only entry whose path or digest moved, and one entry was added. repairVerification.finding: CLAUDE-V3-S1 — unicode-norm-duplicate masked by the entrypoint-absent arm
repairVerification.status: REPAIRED — FULLY, by the remedy I specified and without touching the frozen bytes
repairVerification.howIMeasuredIt: I parsed both manifests and extracted the entrypoint and every tree path. The v2/v3 predecessor declares entrypoint 'bin/entry' with tree entries that do not include it, which is what let the entrypoint-presence rule fire and mask the normalization duplicate. The v4 replacement declares the same entrypoint and its tree now contains 'bin/entry', so that rule cannot fire. The NFC/NFD pair survives as the sole violation and is genuinely distinct at the byte level: 62696e2f636166c3a9 against 62696e2f63616665cc81, identical only after NFC normalization. An implementation that checks entrypoint presence and never normalizes paths now fails this fixture, which was the whole point.
repairVerification.methodIsCorrect: The repair does not edit the fixture I objected to. It authors new bytes at fixtures/dr-103.v4/, retargets only this corpus's own entry, and records predecessorV2Path and predecessorV2Sha256 f068504e… so the provenance of the superseded fixture is legible. That respects the do-not-mutate and do-not-retarget constraints simultaneously.

repairVerification.finding: CLAUDE-V3-ADV-1 — parity case authored only the equal-lists arm
repairVerification.howIMeasuredIt: A new authored entry, TC-NAME.reserved-list-live-grammar-parity-mismatch, pins the same index as the passing arm — TC-ACCEPT.index-with-minimal.json in dr-103.v2, reused rather than mutated — against a new observation file whose reservedRootCommands is ['help','version','doctor','analyze'] where the index carries ['help','version','doctor']. I read both operands and confirmed the divergence, and the packet's recorded liveGrammarDigest 32f22cfc… reproduces against the observation bytes. Expected outcome is REFUSE. The original equal-lists arm is retained unchanged at its dr-103.v2 path, so both arms now exist and a checker that never performs the comparison passes one and fails the other.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the unicode repair was cosmetic. The entrypoint now resolves in the tree and the NFC/NFD pair is byte-distinct, so the masking arm cannot fire.

That the new fixture was created by editing the old one. The v2 bytes still hash to the digest the frozen corpora record, and the new file is a separate path with the predecessor's path and digest recorded beside it.

That the mismatch arm reuses the passing arm's grammar file and is therefore not divergent. It pins a different observation file whose list differs by one element, and the packet's digest of that file reproduces.
That a lock fixture is scored under another name. Id-set comparison against deferredUntilDR111 and authored[] refutes it.
That some other authored fixture drifted while attention was on the two repairs. Keyed by id, exactly one entry's path or digest moved.
That a recorded digest somewhere does not reproduce. 52 authored plus 32 supporting plus 162 predecessor-pinned dr-103.v2 measurements all reproduce.
coordinatorNote: This is an ACCEPT of the corpus at the SATISFIED-grade bar, not a disposition of the row. The part worth the coordinator's attention is the repair method: my v3 finding named a fixture that could not be edited, and v4 solved it by authoring new bytes under a new directory, retargeting only its own entry, and recording the superseded path and digest for provenance — which satisfies do-not-mutate and do-not-retarget at the same time and leaves the frozen record legible. I verified that claim the hard way, re-measuring all 162 dr-103.v2 pins that the two frozen corpora record, and the directory is untouched. Both advisories are wording rather than evidence: one is an inherited line, identical in v2, v3 and v4, whose word 'produces' is contradicted by three other statements in the same document and by the structure, and the other is two metadata keys outside a block labelled closed whose actual closure claim is narrower and true. Neither affects a fixture, a digest, or a scored outcome. DR-103 remains OPEN, the corpus remains unexecuted, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
